reading: The coloured block at the left edge is copied flush to the right edge, and the gap between the two copies is filled, row by row, with that row's first-cell colour.

slots.pattern: the multi-coloured block at the left edge (its first and last columns match)
slots.placement: a copy flush against the right border
slots.filler: each row's leftmost colour fills the background between the two copies

why: output row = block + row[0] repeated + block, on every pair

reading: Each solid 8 rectangle is recoloured by position: an inner core inset by 2 cells becomes 4, and the remaining 2-wide rim is split into quadrants: top-left 6, top-right 1, bottom-left 2, bottom-right 3.

slots.subject: each solid rectangle object
slots.core: cells at least 2 from the rectangle edge -> 4
slots.quadrants: rim cells by half: TL 6, TR 1, BL 2, BR 3

why: every 8 cell is recoloured by its position in its rectangle; background unchanged

reading: Two opposite border lines have different colours; each 1 cell gets one new cell next to it, on the side towards the nearer border line, in that border's colour.

slots.subject: each isolated 1 cell
slots.direction: toward the nearer of the two full border lines

why: every 1 cell gains exactly one neighbour coloured like its nearer border

reading: Each object moves right by a distance equal to its own width.
why: each object keeps its shape and rows; its column offset equals its width

reading: Several noisy copies of one octagonal ring shape, each in its own colour, overlap in a chain among scattered noise cells; the output stacks a clean 6x6 ring of each ring colour vertically, in chain order.
verb: list ring colours as clean rings

slots.shape: the fixed 6x6 octagonal ring (learned from the outputs)
slots.items: the colours that form rings (not the scattered noise colours)
slots.order: along the chain of overlapping rings (the first in order looks like the most intact / top ring; exact rule unclear)

why: output is a 6-wide column of clean rings, one per ring colour

reading: The 2x2 block of four colours at the centre of a 4x4 grid is pulled apart: each cell moves diagonally out to the grid corner nearest it.

slots.subject: each of the four centre cells
slots.target: the grid corner on its diagonal

why: the four colours appear only at the four corners, each at its own diagonal corner

reading: Every 3 cell that has a 3 as an orthogonal neighbour (i.e. belongs to a 4-connected group of 2 or more) becomes 8; lone 3s stay.

new_rows.name: paired
new_rows.datalog:
paired(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DY = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
paired(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), off(DY, DX), DX = 0, Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).

why: key 3->8 on cells with a same-colour 4-neighbour; diagonal-only contact does not count

reading: A vertical and a horizontal line cross; a 3x3 square ring of 4 is drawn around the crossing cell, whose own colour is kept.

new_rows.name: cross
new_rows.datalog: cross(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Ya = Y - 1, cell(Ya, X, C1), Yb = Y + 1, cell(Yb, X, C2), Xa = X - 1, cell(Y, Xa, C3), Xb = X + 1, cell(Y, Xb, C4).

why: the 8 cells around the crossing become 4; the crossing cell and all other cells are unchanged

reading: Two 3x3 boxes of 2 with a 5 centre each have one open side; the openings are filled with 4 and joined by a solid 4 rectangle spanning from just outside one opening to just outside the other, except cells lying behind either box.

slots.ends: the gap cell of each box and the cell just outside it
slots.region: the bounding rectangle of the two outside cells, minus the box cells and the cells behind each box (on its closed side)

why: only background cells inside the bridge become 4; the boxes are unchanged

reading: From the single 2 on the bottom row a two-cell-wide diagonal band of 2 runs up and to the right until the border; where a 1 blocks it, the band steps right past the 1 (the row below gains a cell to bridge it) and goes on.
verb: draw thick diagonal ray around obstacles

slots.source: the 2 cell on the bottom row
slots.direction: up-right, each row offset by one column, two cells wide
slots.obstacle: 1 cells: the band shifts right just past them

why: the band never overwrites a 1 and reaches the border
